text:
incidents-bot: PAGER — severity: high — potential cross-tenant data exposure detected on dedicated-pool:dedicated-209. Automated heuristic flagged overlapping KV cache reads between tenant namespaces. Please acknowledge and join thread. (pager id: pgr-9f2a) :rotating_light:

oncall-ryan: acked. I'm on it. grabbing logs now.

maria-eng: tagging in — if this is KV cache -> possible stale prefix leakage. any proxied routing changes in the last 6h?

elaine-sre: looking at routing events, nothing obvious. but I see burst of GETs with duplicated prefix IDs hitting multiple pods in pool dedicated-209 around 2410001120. patching in a dump now.

raj-security: if confirmed cross-tenant reads, escalate to security immediately. collect sample payloads and mask PII before sharing. Sophia, any support tickets?

sophia-cs: received inbound from cust: enterprise-acme — they saw data from another namespace in SDK responses. Customer asked for timeline and mitigation. I told them we were investigating and would update within 30m.

oncall-ryan: command run: ```kubectl -n redwood get pods -l pool=dedicated-209 -o wide``` shows 12 pods, rolling redeploy in last 2hrs on 4 nodes. Im ssh-ing to node-5 to grab /var/log/redwood/runtime.log tail.

devops-bot: syslog snippet from node-5 (2410001118): ```[runtime] kvcache: serving prefix \"ns/tenant-117/conv/\" to client 10.2.8.12; cache-hit=true; origin-pool=dedicated-209 
[router] route-assigned: tenant=117 -> shard=shard-43 on node-5 
[router] route-assigned: tenant=701 -> shard=shard-43 on node-7```

maria-eng: that log line looks like shard-43 is serving multiple tenant prefixes concurrently. we should check our namespace->shard assignment table. possible cause: stale routing snapshot on node-7 after partial rollout.

elaine-sre: running quick verification: ```select tenant, shard, last_sync from routing_snapshot where shard='shard-43';``` returns tenant:117 last_sync:2410000400, tenant:701 last_sync:2410001085. mismatch window.

raj-security: collect affected sample responses. redact then store into secure evidence bucket. do NOT paste raw PII into slack. Use secure link.

oncall-ryan: temporary mitigation proposal: 1) cordon node-5 and node-7 from serving routing table (evict new assignments) 2) force global routing snapshot refresh 3) evict KV cache entries for shard-43 across nodes 4) fail traffic for affected tenants to fallback model in another pool. Who can run?

maria-eng: I can trigger routing refresh and evict cache entries. sequence: ```./rctl routing refresh --shard shard-43 --force && ./rctl kv evict --shard shard-43 --all-nodes``` 

elaine-sre: cordon commands: ```kubectl cordon node-5 && kubectl cordon node-7``` then remove from loadbalancer. I'll take that.

devops-bot: NOTE: there is a running rollout of runtime v2.14 on 4 pods. cordoning will slow rollout but mitigations higher priority.

oncall-ryan: please also set an emergency route policy to divert traffic for tenants 117 and 701 to dedicated-307 (isolated pool). `routebox set --tenant 117,701 --pool dedicated-307 --ttl 1800`

maria-eng: evict job started at 2410001299. est ~45s per node. watching logs.

elaine-sre: nodes cordoned and removed from LB at 2410001308.

devops-bot: eviction progress: node-5: done, node-7: done, node-3: no entries for shard-43.

maria-eng: routing snapshot refresh completed at 2410001326. verification query now returns single-tenant mapping for shard-43 (tenant-701 only). going to re-run consistency check across control-plane.

raj-security: good. Sophia, please let customer know we have isolated the pool, evicted cache, and launched failover. Provide ETA for full remediation after post-incident review. Keep them in the loop but avoid raw logs.

sophia-cs: messaging drafted: \"We've isolated the affected pool and performed an immediate cache eviction and routing refresh. We've failed traffic to an isolated pool to prevent further cross-namespace reads. Our security and engineering teams are collecting evidence and will follow up with details and remediation timeline within 2 hours.\" sending now.

oncall-ryan: quick evidence capture commands: ```journalctl -u redwood-runtime -o short-iso | grep shard-43 | head -n 300 > /tmp/evidence-shard43.log && aws s3 cp /tmp/evidence-shard43.log s3://secure-evidence/pgr-9f2a/``` encrypted upload in progress.

maria-eng: verification of responses from tenant-117 after failover: sampling 50 replies, none show foreign namespace IDs. running quality checks for regressions due to failover.

raj-security: start an incident ticket in the security tracker with severity P0 and attach the S3 evidence link. Also flag for potential customer notification template if PII confirmed.

sophia-cs: customer acknowledged our mitigation and asked for root cause. they want to know: \"Was any persisted data from our namespace read by another tenant?\" -> we cannot confirm yet. collecting.

elaine-sre: early hypothesis: partial control-plane snapshot during rolling rollout allowed two tenants to be assigned to same shard briefly. KV cache lacked strict namespace prefix validation in runtime v2.14 for cross-shard reads. We'll confirm.

maria-eng: immediate next steps (owners): - evidence upload: ryan (done uploading) - runtime log diff and replay: maria - routing consistency audit across last 24h: elaine - security triage & PII assessment: raj - CS comms ongoing: sophia

devops-bot: escalation reminder: open PDR (post-incident detection) and schedule live incident bridge if it goes >60m.

oncall-ryan: creating incident bridge now and paging infra leads. bridge link: https://zoom.redwood/bridge/pgr-9f2a

maria-eng: log analysis shows 23 requests around 2410001119 where response headers included X-namespace:tenant-701 while auth token mapped to tenant-117. grabbing samples into evidence bucket (redacted).

raj-security: initial assessment: potential data exposure window approx 2410001118-2410001130. scope unknown. prioritize customers with high-sensitivity data.

sophia-cs: notified legal and account management for enterprise-acme. they're asking for immediate notification of any confirmed PII exposures.

elaine-sre: rollback plan: either rollback runtime to v2.13 on affected pool or backfill strict namespace check into v2.14 and deploy hotfix. rollback is faster. maria, can you coordinate?

maria-eng: I can push rollback to v2.13 on dedicated-209 in a controlled manner: ```deployctl rollback --pool dedicated-209 --version v2.13 --grace 60``` will take ~8min. need approval to proceed.

oncall-ryan: approve rollback. prioritize containment.

maria-eng: rollback started at 2410001420. monitoring.

devops-bot: alert: rollback initiated. beware metrics noise.

maria-eng: rollback completed at 2410001702. post-rollback verification: no further cross-tenant indicators in runtime logs. routing snapshots stable.

raj-security: continue evidence analysis. open items: 1) exact list of affected tenants and token mappings 2) confirm data types in sample responses 3) retention and deletion plan for exposed artifacts 4) timeline for customer notification.

sophia-cs: will coordinate customer notification and legal. we've committed to update enterprise-acme within 2 hours and share an initial technical statement.

oncall-ryan: handing off active ownership to maria for remediation and postmortem. I'll stay on bridge for 30m for any followups.

maria-eng: taking ownership. I'll produce a short incident report and remediation PR for the runtime hotfix. Expect a root-cause writeup in 24h and full postmortem in 72h.

raj-security: adding incident to security on-call queue for deeper forensic. link to evidence: s3://secure-evidence/pgr-9f2a/evidence-shard43.log (redacted copy).

sophia-cs: closing the customer loop for now — they've acknowledged our containment steps and are awaiting the 2h update.

incidents-bot: Incident pgr-9f2a status: mitigated (failover + rollback), owners: maria-eng, raj-security, sophia-cs. Reminder: tag with #customer-impact and schedule 72h postmortem. :white_check_mark:

maria-eng: quick note for postmortem: include stash of commands used, timeline, control-plane snapshot race condition analysis, and a mitigation plan: 1) strict runtime-level namespace validation 2) routing snapshot verification barrier before rollout 3) automated bloom-filter checks to detect cross-namespace reads in real time.

elaine-sre: adding instrumentation task: emit per-request namespace auth->response namespace mismatch metric. we'll use that to alert earlier.

raj-security: I'll draft immediate customer-safe technical summary for legal review.

oncall-ryan: thanks team. handing off.

maria-eng: logged action items into incident board. will follow up with timeline and PRs.

sophia-cs: will send scheduled customer update at 2410002434 (2h).

incidents-bot: THREAD CLOSED — mitigation in place, remediation in progress. Remember to tag with incident-ownership and follow postmortem timeline.
